items.name: AgentCourt (adversarial evolvable lawyer agents)
items.what_agents_must_do: Play opposing lawyer agents through full simulated civil trials, accumulating experience/case/code databases via self-reflection; evolved agents are then scored on CourtBench and by professional lawyers on cognitive agility, professional knowledge, logical rigor.
task_families: adversarial courtroom simulation (evolvable lawyer agents vs judge/plaintiff/defendant roles)
items.size: courtroom simulation framework with granular annotations across trial stages; 1,000 simulated civil cases for adversarial evolution; CourtBench evaluation set
items.world_requirements: Adversarial matter shape: two agent seats (our side / opposing counsel) attached to one matter, a scripted judge NPC, per-round debate transcripts persisted as matter documents, and a growing firm knowledge base the agent may write to — the self-evolution loop maps directly onto a firm world's precedent/playbook stores; grading needs lawyer-rubric LLM-judge plus win/loss outcome fields.

items.name: AgentsCourt / SimuCourt (+ Legal-KB)
items.what_agents_must_do: Act as the judge: consume indictments, defendant statements and facts, simulate/observe court debate, retrieve from a legal knowledge base, and produce the judgment (facts findings, applicable law, verdict), compared against real first/second-instance judgments.
task_families: judicial decision-making from case materials (court debate simulation → precedent/legal retrieval → judgment drafting)
items.size: SimuCourt: 420 Chinese judgment documents across 3 case types (first-instance, second-instance, retrial); 420 real judgment documents (criminal/civil/administrative; first + second instance) + JudicialKB knowledge base
items.world_requirements: A courtroom module bolted onto the firm world: case-bundle documents per matter (indictment, statements, facts), a retrieval tool over a statute+precedent KB (JudicialKB analogue), multi-role scripted participants (prosecutor/defense as NPC agents), and grading that compares generated judgments to the real gold judgment on verdict match (deterministic) + reasoning quality (judge-graded); second-instance cases add an appeal-chain task shape.

items.name: ALKiln (SuffolkLITLab/ALKiln)
items.what_agents_must_do: Automated end-to-end testing of docassemble interviews: Gherkin scenarios drive a headless browser (puppeteer/cucumber) through the interview, set fields, assert reached screens and generated documents; includes constrained-random input testing. Agents can be tasked with writing tests that catch seeded interview bugs, or fixing interviews until suites pass.
task_families: write Gherkin tests for an interview
diagnose/fix interview logic from failing tests
items.size: framework; Gherkin .feature test suites per interview
items.world_requirements: This is directly hostable: a docassemble instance + ALKiln runner as world infrastructure; tasks = interview repo with seeded defects + failing/passing test oracle. Fully deterministic pass/fail grading with zero LLM judging — a rare executable-verifier anchor for legal workflow tasks.

items.name: Crosby Multi-turn Negotiation Bench
items.what_agents_must_do: Perform contract negotiation as a sequence of judgment calls across turns — respond to counterparty redlines, decide concessions, escalate per playbook — measuring senior-commercial-lawyer workflow quality, not isolated clause edits.
items.size: launched June 2026 by law firm Crosby; size undisclosed
items.world_requirements: A counterparty actor that issues redlines over multiple rounds, a negotiation playbook document with escalation thresholds, and a redline diff tool. Complements Harvey LAB's single-turn redline tasks with genuine multi-turn state; grading needs playbook-compliance checks (deterministic where thresholds are numeric).

items.name: Harvey LAB extensions: M&A Due Diligence (+ announced enterprise search, fund formation, investigations/discovery)
items.what_agents_must_do: Agentic M&A due diligence over simulated virtual data rooms: review VDR documents, spot issues, and produce diligence reports; future extensions cover enterprise search, fund formation, investigations and discovery.
items.size: VDR-scale document sets (hundreds–thousands of docs per deal); rollout announced 2026
items.world_requirements: Extends the already-inventoried Harvey LAB: the firm world should plan for VDR-scale document stores (hundreds of files per matter) and diligence-report deliverables with per-issue rubric criteria — watch this repo for direct anchor tasks.

items.name: OpenProBono
items.what_agents_must_do: Open-source legal research agent framework: configurable bots with tool access to trusted legal sources (courts, statutes, web), producing cited research reports for pro bono / access-to-justice use; users pick an agent by practice area and receive a formal cited report.
items.size: open-source platform (backend/API + bots)
items.world_requirements: A world needs a sealed legal-source corpus (statutes, cases, regs) exposed via search/retrieval tools plus a citation-graph table, so research tasks can be graded on (a) correct answer keys and (b) citation validity checked deterministically against the corpus — the OpenProBono bot architecture is the reference tool surface.

items.name: Ready Jurist One / J1Bench (J1-EVAL, FudanDISC)
items.what_agents_must_do: Complete legal tasks through multi-turn interaction with other participants under procedural rules across six environments; dual automated + human evaluation. Note: 'Ready Jurist One' (arXiv 2507.04037) is the paper behind the J1Bench/J1-EVAL entry already in the inventory — same FudanDISC project, not a new item.
task_families: interactive legal-intelligence tasks in dynamic multi-participant environments
items.size: 6 interactive scenarios; 508 evaluation environments (160 L1 / 186 L2 / 192 L3); 17 agents tested; 6 interactive legal environments; dynamic multi-level tasks
items.world_requirements: Already the inventory's closest analogue: confirms the design pattern of procedural multi-participant environments with graded interaction; lawfirm-qwen's differentiator remains the executable filesystem/tool world and deterministic boundary-proven grading, which J1-EVAL lacks.

items.name: TERMS-Bench
items.what_agents_must_do: Negotiate in a bilateral game with private reservation values where the environment itself is the verifier — welfare/surplus outcomes are computed exactly, diagnosing strategic reasoning beyond deal rate.
items.size: Bayesian-game bilateral price negotiation testbed; 13 LLM agents evaluated
items.world_requirements: Not legal-specific, but the design pattern matters: give the counterparty a hidden reservation value and score the agent on computed surplus — a fully deterministic verifier for negotiation tasks the law-firm world could adopt for settlement/deal-term negotiation tasks.

items.name: ACORD (Atticus Clause Retrieval Dataset)
items.what_agents_must_do: Given a clause-drafting query (e.g., 'MFN clause favoring customer'), retrieve and rank the most relevant precedent clauses from a corpus; graded against complete expert star-ratings including annotated zero-relevance negatives (NDCG@k).
task_families: precedent clause retrieval for contract drafting
items.size: 114 queries, 126,000+ expert-ranked query-clause pairs (1–5 stars), ACL 2025
items.world_requirements: A clause-bank/precedent-library table (clause text, type, source agreement, quality rank) with a retrieval tool. Task shape maps directly to a firm world: 'pull the three best indemnification precedents from the firm knowledge base before drafting' — deterministic grading via gold rankings makes it one of the best verifiable sub-steps to embed inside a larger drafting task.

items.name: ArabLegalEval
items.what_agents_must_do: Answer Arabic legal QA across native Saudi-regulation tasks and translated reasoning tasks; automatic grading.
items.size: multitask QA benchmark from Saudi legal documents + translated MMLU/LegalBench items
items.world_requirements: MCQ/QA tables; jurisdiction-expansion material with a synthetic-QA-from-regulations generation pipeline worth borrowing for authoring new firm-world tasks from any regulation set.

items.name: BSARD (Belgian Statutory Article Retrieval Dataset)
items.what_agents_must_do: Given a French-language legal question from a Belgian citizen, retrieve the relevant statutory articles from a 22.6k-article corpus (best baseline 74.8% R@100). Graded by recall@k/MAP against jurist labels.
task_families: statutory article retrieval for citizen questions
items.size: 1,108+ questions labeled against 22,600+ Belgian law articles; 1,100+ citizen legal questions; corpus of 22,600+ Belgian statutory articles; jurist-labeled
items.world_requirements: French-language statute-research shape: statute table (article_id, code, text) with search tool; research tickets carrying a client question and gold article-ID sets; deterministic recall/precision grader; directly parallel to COLIEE Task 3 so one world 'statute research' task shape can host both EN/JA and FR instantiations.

items.name: CALRK-Bench
items.what_agents_must_do: Answer Korean legal questions requiring context-aware reasoning — applying provided statutory/case context rather than parametric recall.
items.size: context-aware legal reasoning benchmark for Korean law (2026)
items.world_requirements: Provided-context QA pairs with deterministic answers; a template for 'reason only from the matter file' tasks that punish parametric-knowledge shortcuts.

items.name: CaseGen (multi-stage Chinese legal case document generation)
items.what_agents_must_do: Given staged case materials, generate four successive litigation documents (defense statement → trial facts → reasoning → judgment), evaluated with LLM-as-judge plus human annotation; errors propagate across stages.
items.size: ~500 real cases, 4 chained generation stages
items.world_requirements: The closest published analogue to lawfirm-qwen's chained-matter shape: a matter lifecycle with 4 sequential deliverable slots, each stage consuming the prior stage's output as input documents; world needs per-stage reference documents and rubric-based LLM-judge grading, plus lifecycle state tracking so stage-N tasks unlock only after stage-N-1 filing — enables measuring error amplification like LegalWorld.

items.name: Chinese Labor Law LLM Benchmark
items.what_agents_must_do: Answer and analyze Chinese labor-law questions/disputes (employment contracts, dismissal, compensation), testing a single practice vertical in depth rather than breadth.
task_families: labor-law QA and case analysis (domain-vertical evaluation)
items.size: labor-law-specialized task set (2026)
items.world_requirements: Evidence that practice-area verticals are benchmarkable: the world's employment-law department can host a labor-specific ticket family (dismissal-risk memos, severance computations with gold amounts, contract-clause compliance checks against a labor-statute table); computations graded numerically, citations by set match.

items.name: ContractEval
items.what_agents_must_do: Clause-level legal-risk identification in commercial contracts: for each of 41 CUAD risk categories, locate the relevant clause or correctly answer 'no related clause'; scored on F1, Jaccard span overlap, and a 'laziness' rate (wrongly answering no-clause).
items.size: CUAD test split (102 contracts × 41 risk categories), 19 models evaluated; NLLP 2025, arXiv:2508.03080; CUAD test set repackaged; 41 risk categories; 19 models evaluated
items.world_requirements: Same substrate as CUAD (already in inventory) — full contract documents in a matter folder — but reframed for generative LLMs with the laziness metric. A firm world hosts it as 'review the counterparty draft and flag all 41 checklist risks'; verifier is span-overlap against gold, plus a penalty channel for omission, which is a good flakiness probe.

items.name: DISC-Law-Eval (DISC-LawLLM evaluation suite)
items.what_agents_must_do: Answer exam-derived objective questions and open-ended legal-service questions (consultation, analysis); objective part exact-match, subjective part GPT-judge scored on accuracy/completeness/clarity.
task_families: objective legal MCQ (single/multi answer, 3 difficulty bands)
subjective legal QA graded by LLM judge
items.size: objective MCQ set (multi-difficulty, from Chinese legal exams) + subjective QA set
items.world_requirements: Same certification-exam shape as JEC-QA plus a client-consultation ticket shape: consultation tickets with reference answers and a rubric (accuracy/completeness/clarity) for LLM-judge grading; world needs a judge-prompt harness and reference-answer storage per ticket, alongside the deterministic MCQ table.

items.name: DLawBench
items.what_agents_must_do: Evaluate LLMs through multi-turn legal consultation service dialogues — eliciting missing facts from the client, maintaining consistency, and delivering correct advice across turns.
items.size: multi-turn legal consultation benchmark (2026)
items.world_requirements: A simulated-client actor with a hidden fact sheet the agent must elicit — the tau-bench user-simulator pattern applied to legal intake. The firm world needs client personas with withheld facts and grading on whether the agent asked the right questions before advising.

items.name: GerDaLIR (German Dataset for Legal Information Retrieval)
items.what_agents_must_do: Given a passage that (in the source) cited one or more cases, retrieve the referenced decisions from a 131k-document German case corpus. Graded by recall@k/MRR against citation-derived labels.
items.size: GerDaLIR: 123k+ retrieval queries from German case law; LegalQuAD: 200 QA pairs; BenGER (arXiv:2605.28183): subsumption-based reasoning; GerLeRB: legislative retrieval; 123k queries, 144k relevance labels, 131k documents (Open Legal Data)
items.world_requirements: German-practice library: a large precedent table with full decision texts and a search tool; task shape = 'find the authority this draft passage should cite' — the agent gets a brief passage from a matter document and must return case IDs; deterministic recall@k grader against the gold citation set; large label volume makes it ideal for auto-generating many world tasks.

items.name: Hallucination-detection cluster 2026 (Who Checks the Citations?; LegalHalluLens; Source or It Didn't Happen)
items.what_agents_must_do: Detect whether cited cases/statutes exist and support the stated propositions; typed hallucination taxonomies; multi-agent debate/verification frameworks scored against gold labels.
items.size: three 2026 arXiv benchmarks (2606.21155, 2606.18021, 2605.08583) for detecting legal citation hallucination
items.world_requirements: Gold authority tables (real vs fabricated citations with support labels). The firm world can inject fabricated authorities into matter files as canary probes and deterministically check whether agents catch or propagate them.

items.name: IL-TUR (Indian Legal Text Understanding and Reasoning)
items.what_agents_must_do: Complete eight India-specific legal NLP tasks spanning extraction, sentence-role structuring, outcome/bail prediction, statute identification, precedent retrieval and summarization, monolingual (EN/HI) and multilingual. Per-task automatic metrics with a public leaderboard.
task_families: rhetorical role labeling of judgment sentences
items.size: 8 tasks over Indian legal documents; 8 tasks with leaderboard (ACL 2024)
items.world_requirements: An India-desk bundle reusing existing shapes: NER→citation-index, rhetorical roles→'structure this judgment into facts/arguments/ruling sections' (sentence-label table with gold roles), bail prediction→intake-risk memo with gold binary column, statute ID→statute-table set match, PCR→precedent-retrieval with gold cited-case sets, summarization→reference-based grading; needs Hindi/Indic text support in the world's document store and graders.

items.name: JBE-QA
items.what_agents_must_do: Answer Japanese bar-examination questions assessing legal domain knowledge; deterministic MCQ grading.
items.size: Japanese bar exam QA dataset (2025)
items.world_requirements: MCQ table + exact-match grader; jurisdiction-expansion material only.

items.name: JEC-QA (thunlp)
items.what_agents_must_do: Answer Chinese bar-exam multiple-choice/multi-answer questions, optionally retrieving relevant legal articles first; requires multi-step legal reasoning (SOTA ~28% vs 81% skilled humans at publication). Exact-match graded.
task_families: case-analysis bar-exam MCQ (with retrieval over legal materials)
items.size: 26,365 MCQ from China's National Judicial Examination; 26,365 multiple-choice/multiple-answer questions (Chinese National Judicial Examination)
items.world_requirements: Associate-certification task shape: a 'training/qualification' module in the firm world where agents must pass exam batches before unlocking matter work; needs a questions table (stem, options, gold answer set, KD/CA type tag) plus an optional legal-materials retrieval tool; grading is exact set-match on chosen options — fully deterministic and cheap.

items.name: KBL (Korean Benchmark for Legal Language Understanding)
items.what_agents_must_do: Korean legal knowledge and reasoning QA including the full Korean bar exam, evaluable open-book (with statute/precedent corpus) or closed-book.
items.size: 7 knowledge tasks (510 ex) + 4 reasoning tasks (288 ex) + Korean bar exam (4 domains, 53 tasks, 2,510 ex)
items.world_requirements: MCQ bank + optional retrieval corpus; the open-book/closed-book toggle is the reusable design — the firm world can score every knowledge task both with and without its research tools to attribute performance to tooling.

items.name: KoBLEX
items.what_agents_must_do: Multi-hop open legal QA over Korean statutes: chain provisions across articles to answer, with provision-level gold supporting evidence.
items.size: open legal QA with multi-hop statutory reasoning (2025)
items.world_requirements: Statutes table with cross-reference links and multi-hop gold chains; the hop-chain gold pattern maps to the firm world's multi-step research tasks where intermediate lookups are verifiable (like LegalAgentBench's key_middle).

items.name: Korean Canonical Legal Benchmark
items.what_agents_must_do: Test legal reasoning with all needed rules supplied in-context, isolating reasoning ability from memorized Korean law knowledge.
items.size: knowledge-independent legal reasoning items (2025)
items.world_requirements: Self-contained rule+facts→conclusion items with exact answers; ideal deterministic filler tasks for the firm world that work in any jurisdiction because the rules ship with the task.

items.name: LAiW (Chinese Legal LLM Benchmark)
items.what_agents_must_do: Complete 14 Chinese legal tasks arranged by syllogistic reasoning depth, from basic extraction/retrieval to full legal application; automated per-task metrics. Designed to test whether LLMs follow legal-practice logic bottom-up.
task_families: basic information retrieval (NER, article recommendation, element recognition)
legal foundation inference (similar case matching, controversy focus mining, charge prediction)
complex legal application (judgment prediction, judicial summarization, consultation)
items.size: 14 tasks in 3 levels (BIR/LFI/CLA)
items.world_requirements: A leveled task ladder in the world: tier-1 tasks (extract entities/elements from a filed document, recommend statute IDs), tier-2 (match precedents, identify dispute focus), tier-3 (draft judgment-prediction or consultation memos); world needs the same statute/precedent tables as CAIL shapes plus per-tier gold labels, and a progression rule that gates tier-3 matters on tier-1/2 pass rates — directly mirrors LAiW's claim that models skip basics.

items.name: LBox Open (Korean legal benchmark)
items.what_agents_must_do: From Korean case fact descriptions, predict case names, applicable statutes, criminal sentence categories and civil claim-acceptance levels, and summarize Supreme Court precedents. Deterministic classification metrics + ROUGE.
items.size: 147k-precedent corpus; tasks: case-name cls 11.3k, statute cls 2.8k, criminal LJP, civil LJP, summarization 20k (51k+ variant)
items.world_requirements: Korean-desk instantiation of the intake-assessment shape: matters with Korean fact narratives and gold columns (case_name, statute_ids[], sentence bucket, claim-acceptance ratio); statute lookup tool over Korean codes; summarization tasks graded against reference summaries; demonstrates the same shapes as CAIL/LBox generalize across CJK jurisdictions with only table/language swaps.

items.name: Legal RAG Bench (Isaacus)
items.what_agents_must_do: End-to-end RAG: retrieve the gold passage and generate an expert-level long-form answer; full-factorial design decomposes errors into retrieval failures vs reasoning failures vs hallucinations.
items.size: 4,876 passages (Victorian Criminal Charge Book) + 100 expert questions with long-form answers and gold supporting passages; arXiv:2603.01710
items.world_requirements: A firm knowledge-base tool over a chunked practice manual with per-question gold passage IDs. The error-decomposition protocol (retrieval ceiling analysis) is the transferable asset: a simulation world can adopt the same hierarchical error taxonomy to attribute agent task failures to tool-use vs reasoning.

items.name: LegalCiteBench
items.what_agents_must_do: Closed-book and tool-assisted citation reliability: retrieve correct citations, complete partial citations, detect citation errors, match cases to propositions, and verify/correct case support. Deterministic gold from real reporters.
items.size: 1,000 root cases → 23,646 evaluation instances, 5 task families; ICML 2026 AI4Law
items.world_requirements: A citator tool backed by a case table (name, reporter cite, holding, treatment) — the world's 'Westlaw'. Task shape: cite-check a draft brief; grading is exact-match on citation strings and support labels. Directly hostable as a verifiable QA gate on any drafting task the firm world already runs.

items.name: LegalEval (SemEval-2023 Task 6)
items.what_agents_must_do: Segment judgments into rhetorical roles (preamble/facts/ratio/arguments), extract legal named entities, and predict case outcomes with explanations (CJPE).
items.size: 3 subtasks over Indian court judgments; 26 participating teams
items.world_requirements: Judgment documents with sentence-level gold labels; hostable as litigation-analysis subtasks (structure an opinion before summarizing it) with deterministic per-sentence grading.

items.name: LegalEval-Q
items.what_agents_must_do: Assess/regress the quality (clarity, coherence, terminology) of LLM-generated legal text — a judge-calibration resource rather than an agent task set.
items.size: quality-evaluation benchmark for LLM-generated legal text (2025)
items.world_requirements: Useful for calibrating the firm world's LLM judge: gold quality ratings let you validate that the judge's style/quality criteria correlate with human legal-writing judgments.

items.name: LegalHalBench
items.what_agents_must_do: Answer legal questions while automatic metrics detect common hallucination types (fabricated statutes, misapplied law); paired with factuality fine-tuning methods.
items.size: hallucination benchmark spanning 7 Chinese civil/criminal law areas + 3 automatic metrics
items.world_requirements: A statute ground-truth table to verify every statute the agent cites exists and says what's claimed — an automatic hallucination detector the firm world can run over any deliverable that cites law.

items.name: LegalLens (2024 shared task)
items.what_agents_must_do: Detect legal violations in wild text: extract entities (law, violation, violator, victim) and match violations to affected-class complaints/resolutions via NLI.
items.size: NER + NLI datasets for legal violation identification in unstructured text; best NER F1 ~60%
items.world_requirements: Hostable as class-action intake triage: an inbox of consumer complaints, an entity-extraction deliverable with F1 grading against gold spans, and a matching table linking complaints to open matters. Deterministic span/label grading.

items.name: LexGenius
items.what_agents_must_do: Expert-level Chinese legal general-intelligence MCQ spanning understanding, reasoning, ethics, and procedural judgment, built from recent cases to reduce contamination; best models trail human lawyers.
items.size: 7 dimensions × 11 tasks × 20 abilities; MCQ from recent cases and exams; 12 SOTA LLMs evaluated
items.world_requirements: Static MCQ — hostable only as a knowledge-check layer (e.g., associate 'training quizzes' inside the world); its Dimension-Task-Ability matrix is a useful capability taxonomy for tagging the world's tasks.

items.name: LexRAG
items.what_agents_must_do: Multi-turn legal consultation with retrieval: track evolving client context across 5 dialogue rounds, retrieve relevant statute articles per turn, and generate grounded responses.
items.size: 1,013 multi-turn consultation dialogues, 5 rounds each + 17,228-article candidate corpus
items.world_requirements: A client-intake dialogue engine (simulated client turns) plus a statutes retrieval tool; grading combines retrieval gold per turn with response metrics. Gives the firm world its 'client consultation' task shape with per-turn verifiable retrieval anchors.

items.name: LexRubric
items.what_agents_must_do: Answer open-ended legal tasks graded against structured diagnostic rubrics that decompose quality into per-dimension criteria, positioning rubric design itself as the evaluation contribution.
task_families: open-ended legal generation with diagnostic rubrics
items.size: rubric-guided diagnostic benchmark for open-ended legal tasks (2026)
items.world_requirements: Another rubric-taxonomy donor: per-dimension diagnostic rubrics (vs Harvey's all-pass binary) let the firm world report which capability dimension failed, improving flaky-task boundary evidence.

items.name: LLeQA
items.what_agents_must_do: Long-form legal QA: retrieve supportive statutory articles from Belgian legislation and generate interpretable, grounded prose answers (retrieve-then-read pipeline).
items.size: 1,868 expert-annotated long-form questions + Belgian statutory corpus
items.world_requirements: Statutes table + retrieval tool + long-form answer grading (article-grounding is the verifiable part). Template for the firm world's 'research memo with pinpoint statutory citations' tasks where cited-article IDs are deterministically checkable.

items.name: Magis-Bench
items.what_agents_must_do: Magistrate-level legal writing: multi-turn discursive analysis and drafting of complete civil and criminal judicial sentences from Brazilian judicial exams; graded by a 4-frontier-model judge panel (Kendall's W 0.984); best model 6.97/10.
items.size: 74 questions from 8 Brazilian magistrate exams (2023-2025); 23 models evaluated
items.world_requirements: Low direct fit (Brazilian judiciary), but its multi-judge-panel grading with reported inter-judge agreement is a robustness upgrade over Harvey LAB's single-judge scheme; a world adopting LLM-judged drafting tasks should replicate the panel + agreement-stat protocol.

items.name: MASLegalBench
items.what_agents_must_do: Multi-agent deductive legal reasoning over GDPR cases using an extended IRAC(+Common Sense) decomposition; designed to test task decomposition and agent specialization in multi-agent systems.
items.size: 950 MCQs from 15 expert-authored GDPR court cases
items.world_requirements: Deterministic MCQ grading; hostable as a data-privacy practice-group task line: world needs GDPR text + case-file documents and supports assigning subtasks to specialist sub-agents; the IRAC step structure gives natural intermediate checkpoints for process grading.

items.name: NitiBench
items.what_agents_must_do: Thai legal QA under RAG and long-context regimes: general financial-law questions plus real tax cases requiring multi-step statutory reasoning; evaluates retriever+LLM frameworks end-to-end.
items.size: NitiBench-CCL (Thai financial law) + NitiBench-Tax (real tax rulings)
items.world_requirements: Statute corpus + gold-cited answers; its RAG-vs-long-context ablation protocol is reusable for deciding which firm-world tasks need retrieval tools vs stuffed context.

items.name: ObliQA / RegNLP RIRAG
items.what_agents_must_do: Regulatory information retrieval and obligation-grounded answer generation: find the passages imposing obligations relevant to a compliance question and synthesize a grounded answer (RePASs metric scores obligation coverage and contradiction).
items.size: 27,869 questions over 40 ADGM financial-regulation documents (~640k words); RIRAG-2025 shared task + ObliQA-MultiPassage extension
items.world_requirements: A regulations corpus tool plus compliance-question task shape: 'what must our client do under these rules?' Gold passage IDs give the verifiable core; RePASs-style obligation-coverage scoring is adoptable for the world's compliance-memo tasks.

items.name: PLawBench
items.what_agents_must_do: Three practitioner task categories — public legal consultation, practical case analysis, legal document generation — each graded by fine-grained expert rubrics via an aligned LLM evaluator; no current model performs strongly.
items.size: 850 questions, 13 practical scenarios, ~12,500 expert rubric items; ACL 2026
items.world_requirements: Harvey-LAB-style rubric grading applied to consultation and case analysis; the firm world can import its rubric taxonomy (issue identification, fact spotting, document coherence) as additional criterion types for its LLM-judge, and its 13 scenario frames as matter templates.

items.name: SARA (StAtutory Reasoning Assessment)
items.what_agents_must_do: Given statute text plus a fact pattern, determine entailment or compute exact tax liability; ground truth exists as executable Prolog rules, enabling fully deterministic verification of multi-step statutory application.
items.size: 9 simplified IRC sections, 376 cases (276 entailment + 100 numeric) with Prolog gold representations
items.world_requirements: A statutes/rules document set plus client fact-pattern intake records; task shape 'compute the client's liability under these sections and show which subsections applied'. Verifier is exact-dollar comparison (±10% variant used in LegalBench) or Prolog execution — no judge needed. Note: sara_entailment/sara_numeric slices already appear inside LegalBench (inventory item), but the standalone corpus with Prolog gold is richer.

items.name: STARD
items.what_agents_must_do: Retrieve relevant Chinese statutes for authentic layperson queries (vs professional-phrased queries), stressing the vocabulary gap between clients and legal text.
items.size: 1,543 real non-professional queries labeled against 55,348 statute candidates
items.world_requirements: Same substrate as BSARD; its distinctive asset is client-voice query phrasing — useful for making the firm world's simulated-client messages realistically non-legal while keeping retrieval gold verifiable.

items.name: Summarization cluster (Multi-LexSum, CaseSumm, EurLexSum, UK/IN-Abs)
items.what_agents_must_do: Produce single- and multi-document case summaries at specified granularities (one sentence to multi-paragraph), graded vs expert-written gold summaries.
items.size: Multi-LexSum: 9,280 expert summaries at 3 granularities over 40k CRLC documents; CaseSumm: 25.6k SCOTUS opinions with syllabuses
items.world_requirements: Matter folders with many source documents plus gold summaries at multiple lengths — maps to the firm world's 'brief the partner in one paragraph / full memo' dual deliverables; grading via reference-based metrics plus judge.

items.name: TAR stopping-rule research line (QBCB, Kneedle, GRLStop, point-process stopping)
items.what_agents_must_do: Decide when to stop a document review while certifying a target recall level (e.g., 80% recall at 95% confidence) using statistical sampling, knee detection, counting processes, or RL — the defensibility question at the heart of TAR practice.
items.size: multiple papers 2023-2026 with shared TREC/RCV1/CLEF collections
items.world_requirements: A crisp deterministic task for the world: agent runs a review campaign, must file a 'certification memo' with a stopping point and stated recall; grader knows true relevance labels and checks whether the certified recall claim held. Needs only the corpus + oracle infrastructure already listed for TREC tasks.

items.name: TREC Legal Track (2006-2011)
items.what_agents_must_do: Given a mock legal complaint and a document request (topic), find all responsive documents in a 685K-doc email corpus at production scale; interactive task adds a topic-authority appeal loop where relevance disputes are adjudicated. This is the founding TAR/predictive-coding evaluation.
items.size: 685,592 docs (EDRM Enron v1: 455,449 emails + 230,143 attachments); ~40+ topics as mock legal complaints
items.world_requirements: A large email+attachment corpus table (custodian, date, thread, SHA1 hash, file type), a mock complaint + document-request text per matter, a search/query tool over the corpus, a coding tool (responsive/non-responsive/privileged per doc), and a grader computing recall/precision/F1 against sealed gold relevance judgments with sampling-based estimation. Deterministic grading if gold labels exist.

items.name: TREC Total Recall Track (2015-2016)
items.what_agents_must_do: Continuous active learning under a simulated-assessor API: the system iteratively submits documents to an oracle that returns gold relevance, and must reach near-total recall with minimum review effort; scored on gain curves (recall vs docs reviewed).
items.size: 290,099 Jeb Bush governor emails; 34 topics
items.world_requirements: A relevance-oracle tool (returns gold label per submitted doc id, with a call counter as the cost meter), corpus table, and deterministic recall@effort grading. Maps perfectly to a law-firm world: 'associate review budget' = oracle calls; agent decides which docs to route to review and when to stop. Fully deterministic and repeatable.

items.name: TriBench-Ko
items.what_agents_must_do: Evaluate LLMs as operational judicial-workflow systems: jurisprudence summarization, precedent retrieval, legal issue extraction, evidence analysis — each jointly scored for deployment risks (hallucination, omission, bias, prompt sensitivity, non-determinism, adjudicative overreach).
items.size: 1,414 binary items; 4 tasks × risk categories × 10 legal domains; arXiv:2605.03792
items.world_requirements: Its risk-audit matrix is the transferable design: the firm world can attach risk-channel probes (rerun with perturbed prompts, measure non-determinism/omission) to existing tasks — directly relevant to boundary-proving flaky tasks.

items.name: CAIL (China AI & Law Challenge, 2018–2025 umbrella)
items.what_agents_must_do: Per-track: read Chinese criminal/civil case fact descriptions and predict applicable statutes, charges and sentences; match/retrieve similar cases; extract case elements and events; answer bar-exam questions; summarize judgments; analyze argument pairs. Grading is deterministic (accuracy/F1/ROUGE) against gold labels per track.
task_families: legal judgment prediction (law article / charge / prison term)
similar case matching & 类案检索 case retrieval (lajs)
items.size: CAIL2018: 2.68M criminal cases; later years add tracks (similar case matching 8.9k triplets, reading comprehension ~50k, argument mining, summarization, judicial exam); CAIL2024/2025 repos exist; CAIL2018: 2.6M criminal cases; CAIL-Long: 1.13M criminal + 1.10M civil; annual multi-track editions through CAIL2025; 9 GitHub year-repos; tracks change yearly; CAIL2018 alone 2.68M cases, 601 teams
items.world_requirements: A Chinese-law wing of the firm world: a criminal/civil docket table where each matter row carries a fact-description document plus hidden gold fields (statute IDs, charge labels, sentence months, element tags, event spans); a statute table (刑法/民法典 articles with IDs) exposed via a lookup tool; a precedent database with a similarity-search tool for SCM/lajs-shaped tasks; task shapes = intake-assessment memos whose required fields (predicted charge, cited article IDs, sentence range, matched precedent IDs) are graded deterministically against the gold columns.

items.name: COLIEE (Competition on Legal Information Extraction/Entailment)
items.what_agents_must_do: Four standing tasks: retrieve precedent cases supporting a query case (Task 1), decide which paragraphs of a candidate case entail a query fragment (Task 2), retrieve relevant Civil Code statutes for a bar-exam question (Task 3), and answer yes/no statute entailment questions (Task 4); 2025 adds Japanese tort judgment prediction. Best 2025 F1s ~0.33 — still unsolved.
task_families: Task 1: case law retrieval (find noticed/supporting cases for a query case)
Task 2: case entailment (identify the paragraph(s) of a precedent that entail a new-case fragment)
Task 3: statute retrieval (find Civil Code articles relevant to a bar-exam statement)
Task 4: statute entailment (Y/N: does the retrieved article entail the statement)
2025 pilot: legal judgment prediction for Japanese tort cases
items.size: Task1: 650+ queries over ~128k Canadian cases; Task3/4: ~808 Japanese Civil Code questions; annual refresh through 2025 + new Japanese tort LJP pilot; 5 tasks (2026, 13th edition); Canadian Federal Court case corpus + Japanese Civil Code; new tort/rationale-prediction pilot; T1: ~4,400 Canadian Federal Court cases (2023: 959 train / 319 test queries); T3/T4: ~1,000 Japanese Civil Code articles + ~100 new bar-exam questions/year; 24 teams from 13 countries in 2025
items.world_requirements: Two firm-world libraries: (1) a precedent corpus table (thousands of case texts) with a search tool, gold noticed-case lists per query matter — task shape 'compile the table of authorities for this brief', F1-graded; (2) a statute table (Civil Code articles with IDs) with lookup tool, gold relevant-article sets and Y/N entailment labels — task shape 'confirm whether client's position is supported by statute, citing articles'; both need deterministic set-comparison graders and per-task gold-ID columns.

items.name: Philip C. Jessup International Law Moot Court Competition (+ GenAI Jessup study)
items.what_agents_must_do: From the annual Compromis (fixed fictional-state dispute record before the ICJ), draft complete Applicant and Respondent memorials with authority citations; the Charlotin & Ridi study showed LLM memorials blind-scored average-to-superior but with hallucinated citations and shallow analysis.
task_families: written memorial drafting for Applicant and Respondent from a fixed case record
items.size: annual Compromis (agreed case record); ~700 teams; SSRN study: 10 LLM-generated memorials blind-scored by real judges
items.world_requirements: A ready-made 'both-sides drafting' task shape: one matter record, two opposing deliverables (Applicant/Respondent memorials), graded against the published ILSA rubric dimensions via LLM judge plus a deterministic citation-verification pass (every cited authority must exist in the world's authorities table) — the citation-hallucination failure mode the study found is exactly what a closed-world authorities table can verify deterministically.

items.name: Willem C. Vis International Commercial Arbitration Moot
items.what_agents_must_do: Draft Claimant and Respondent memoranda for a fictional international sale-of-goods arbitration (CISG merits + procedural/jurisdiction issues) from a fixed problem record with exhibits and procedural orders.
task_families: memorandum for Claimant and Respondent (CISG + arbitral procedure issues)
items.size: annual Problem (arbitration case record under CISG); ~370+ teams
items.world_requirements: Transactional-disputes variant of the moot shape: problem record decomposed into world documents (contract, correspondence exhibits, procedural orders), a CISG/arbitration-rules statute table for citation verification, two-sided memoranda deliverables scored on issue coverage rubrics; procedural orders arriving mid-task naturally instantiate the world's 'new information drops during the matter' mechanic.

items.name: AnnoCaseLaw
items.what_agents_must_do: Judgment prediction and analysis on negligence cases using detailed factor annotations (duty, breach, causation, damages).
items.size: 471 US Appeals negligence cases with fine-grained annotations
items.world_requirements: Element-level gold annotations enable deterministic grading of issue-element analysis in litigation tasks (did the memo address each negligence element the gold marks present?).

items.name: CAIL2018 (Legal Judgment Prediction dataset)
items.what_agents_must_do: From a criminal case fact description, predict the relevant PRC Criminal Law articles, the charge(s), and the prison term. Deterministically graded (accuracy/F1; sentence within tolerance).
items.size: 2.68M criminal cases (Supreme People's Court published)
items.world_requirements: Criminal-matter intake queue: matters table with fact_description docs and gold columns (article_ids[], charge_labels[], sentence_months); statute lookup tool over a Criminal Law articles table; task shape = charging/sentencing exposure memo with three machine-checkable fields; supports massive task sampling since 2.68M gold-labeled cases exist.

items.name: CAIL2019-SCM (Similar Case Matching)
items.what_agents_must_do: Given a triplet (A,B,C) of private-lending case documents, decide whether B or C is more similar to A. Binary, deterministically graded.
items.size: 8,964 triplets (private-lending cases from China Judgments Online)
items.world_requirements: Precedent-research task shape: a precedents table holding full case texts; a 'compare precedents' assignment where the associate must recommend which of two candidate precedents better supports the client matter; gold binary answer per triplet enables deterministic pass/fail; needs only document storage + read tools.

items.name: CJRC (Chinese Judicial Reading Comprehension, CAIL2019 track)
items.what_agents_must_do: Answer SQuAD-2.0-style questions about a Chinese judgment document: extract answer spans, answer yes/no, or abstain when unanswerable. Graded by EM/F1.
items.size: ~10k judgment documents / ~50k questions (span, yes/no, unanswerable)
items.world_requirements: Document-QA task shape inside the firm: judgment PDFs/texts filed under matters; client-question tickets whose gold answers are spans in the filed document (plus deliberately unanswerable tickets to test abstention); grading via span-overlap F1 — the world needs a per-question gold-span table and a read/grep toolset over matter files.

items.name: Court View Generation corpora (Ye et al. 2018; C3VG-style, CAIL-derived)
items.what_agents_must_do: Generate the court's reasoning section (charge-confirming rationale) from a case fact description. Graded by ROUGE/BLEU vs the real court view, optionally with charge-consistency checks; SCALE's Swiss CVG task is the multilingual analogue.
task_families: court view / judicial rationale generation (本院认为 section)
items.size: ~100k+ fact→court-view pairs across corpora (derived from Chinese criminal judgments)
items.world_requirements: Drafting task shape with reference-based grading: matters carry facts plus a withheld gold rationale text; task = draft the reasoning section of a judgment or an internal 'anticipated court view' memo; world needs a text-similarity grader (ROUGE/BERTScore) plus keyword/charge-consistency checks — the one CAIL-family shape that is generation-graded rather than label-graded.

items.name: EDRM Enron Email Data Set v2
items.what_agents_must_do: The canonical processing-stage corpus: agents ingest PSTs, extract text/metadata, deduplicate by SHA1, family-group attachments, generate EDRM XML load files, and cull by custodian/date — the identification→preservation→collection→processing EDRM stages.
items.size: 1,234,387 emails, 242,800 unique content SHA1s, 151 custodians; PST + EDRM XML load-file formats (~73GB)
items.world_requirements: File-store of raw PST/EML/attachment files with per-file gold metadata (SHA1, custodian, dates, family relationships), tools for extraction and hashing, and deterministic verification: output load file diffed field-by-field against gold EDRM XML; dedupe counts and family integrity checked exactly.

items.name: GerLayQA (German layperson legal QA)
items.what_agents_must_do: Answer real layperson civil-law questions (from Frag-einen-Anwalt.de) with lawyer-quality answers grounded in specific BGB-style code paragraphs; evaluable as paragraph retrieval (deterministic) plus answer quality (judge-graded).
task_families: layperson legal QA with paragraph grounding
layperson question answering grounded in statute paragraphs
items.size: 21,538 layperson questions with lawyer answers grounded to German law-book paragraphs; 21,538 layperson questions with lawyer answers grounded in German legal-code paragraphs
items.world_requirements: Client-intake hotline shape for a German desk: intake tickets with a lay question, gold code-paragraph IDs, and a reference lawyer answer; a statute table of code paragraphs with lookup tool; two-part grading — cited-paragraph set match (deterministic) + answer rubric (LLM judge); 21k items give broad sampling coverage.

items.name: ILDC for CJPE (Indian Legal Documents Corpus)
items.what_agents_must_do: Predict whether an Indian Supreme Court appeal is accepted or rejected from the (decision-stripped) judgment text, and produce explanations compared to expert-marked rationale sentences (best models ~78% vs experts 94%).
items.size: ~35k Indian Supreme Court cases; expert-annotated explanation test set
items.world_requirements: Appellate-risk-assessment shape: matters table of Indian SC case files with the outcome removed and stored as a gold binary column plus gold rationale spans; task = 'advise the client on appeal prospects, citing the passages that drive your view'; grading = binary outcome match (deterministic) + rationale-span overlap (ROUGE/occlusion-style) — gives the world an explanation-graded family.

items.name: LawFlow (minnesotanlp)
items.what_agents_must_do: Captures complete lawyer workflows (from trained law students) on business entity formation: modular, iterative reasoning with revision and client-adaptive strategy — gold process traces, not just outputs; LLM workflows shown to be more rigidly sequential than human ones.
task_families: entity-formation matter handling (intake → structure choice → drafting)
items.size: complete end-to-end workflows from trained law students on business entity formation case studies; 2,009 expert-annotated reasoning actions; end-to-end business-formation workflows (data on HuggingFace)
items.world_requirements: Anchors process-level grading: a world hosting formation matters (client facts table, state filing requirements, operating-agreement templates) can score agents on action-sequence similarity to LawFlow human traces in addition to output correctness — the only public gold-process dataset found for transactional work.

items.name: LawInstruct
items.what_agents_must_do: Training resource, not an eval: instruction-formatted legal QA, summarization, argument mining for domain adaptation studies.
items.size: 58 legal datasets converted to 12M instruction examples, 17 jurisdictions
items.world_requirements: Not hostable as tasks; relevant as training data for a firm-world-native baseline model (lawfirm-qwen fine-tuning) and as a catalog of 58 source datasets to mine for more task shapes.

items.name: LegalQuAD (German legal extractive QA)
items.what_agents_must_do: Answer German legal questions by extracting the answer span from a legal document (or retrieve the right document, in the MTEB variant). EM/F1 or retrieval-metric graded.
task_families: extractive QA over German legal documents
items.size: ~200 question–document pairs (small; also used as an MTEB retrieval task)
items.world_requirements: Small German document-QA ticket shape: client questions each mapped to a filed German statute/decision document and a gold answer span; needs per-ticket gold spans and a span-F1 verifier; too small to carry a task family alone — best used to seed a German-language variant of the CJRC-style ticket shape.

items.name: LeNER-Br (Brazilian legal NER)
items.what_agents_must_do: Tag named entities in Brazilian court and legislation texts, including law-specific classes (Legislation, Jurisprudence). Span-F1 graded.
task_families: legal NER (incl. Legislation and Jurisprudence entity classes)
items.size: 70 documents (66 court, 4 legislation), token-level NER labels
items.world_requirements: Citation-index building shape: task = extract every statute and precedent reference from a filed Brazilian document into a structured citations table; gold token/span annotations per document power a deterministic span-F1 verifier; small size means it seeds a shape rather than a large task pool.

items.name: LEVEN (CAIL2022 legal event detection)
items.what_agents_must_do: Locate event trigger words in Chinese legal case documents and classify each into one of 108 legal event types. Graded by micro/macro F1.
items.size: 8,116 documents, 150,977 event mentions, 108 event types
items.world_requirements: Chronology/issue-coding task shape: matter documents with a hidden gold event-annotation table (doc_id, span, event_type); task = produce a structured case chronology or event log; verifier joins the agent's extracted events against gold spans/types — needs an events schema and span-level deterministic matcher in the world's grading harness.

items.name: MultiEURLEX (multilingual EU-law classification; LEXTREME sub-dataset)
items.what_agents_must_do: Assign EUROVOC concept labels to EU legislative documents in any of 23 languages, including train-on-one-language/test-on-another transfer. Micro/macro-F1 graded.
items.size: 65k EU laws in 23 languages, EUROVOC multi-label
items.world_requirements: Regulatory-watch shape: an EU-legislation feed table where each incoming instrument must be tagged with practice-area/topic labels routed to the right firm team; gold EUROVOC label sets give a deterministic multi-label F1 verifier; already indirectly covered via LEXTREME in the inventory but worth a standalone entry because the routing shape is distinct.

items.name: Pile of Law / MultiLegalPile / LexFiles (corpora)
items.what_agents_must_do: Pretraining/RAG corpora of court opinions, contracts, regulations, administrative documents — no eval tasks of their own.
items.size: 256GB (Pile of Law); 689GB, 24 languages, 17 jurisdictions (MultiLegalPile); LexFiles: 6 English-speaking legal systems
items.world_requirements: Raw material: realistic document filler for the firm world's DMS (making retrieval non-trivial), and source text for authoring new synthetic matters with authentic register.

items.name: Swiss-Judgment-Prediction
items.what_agents_must_do: Predict approval vs dismissal of Swiss Federal Supreme Court cases from multilingual case text (hierarchical BERT ~68–70 macro-F1 in DE/FR). Deterministic binary grading with rich metadata slices.
task_families: robustness/fairness slicing by language, canton, year, legal area
items.size: 85k Swiss Federal Supreme Court cases, 2000–2020, with year/legal-area/canton metadata
items.world_requirements: Multilingual appeal-triage shape: docket rows in three languages with gold outcome column plus metadata columns enabling per-slice scoreboards (language/canton/area) — the metadata makes it uniquely suited to a world that wants fairness/robustness dashboards; only needs document store, gold labels, and slice-aware aggregation in the grader.

items.name: VICTOR (Brazilian Supreme Court document dataset)
items.what_agents_must_do: Classify Brazilian Supreme Court case documents by type and assign process themes (multi-label). Graded by accuracy/F1 against expert annotations.
items.size: 692k+ STF documents, expert-annotated
items.world_requirements: Mailroom/docketing task shape: an inbound-documents queue where each uploaded file must be typed and routed (doc_type field, theme labels) before matter work proceeds; world needs a document-metadata table with hidden gold type/theme columns and a deterministic label-match verifier — a natural 'paralegal ops' family that stress-tests high-volume triage rather than reasoning.

items.name: A2J Author
items.what_agents_must_do: Guided-interview authoring platform (Chicago-Kent/CALI) for self-represented litigants: branching Q&A ('path to the courthouse') that populates HotDocs/LHI court-form templates for filing.
items.size: 1,000+ live guided interviews; used 7M+ times since 2005
items.world_requirements: Same hosting shape as docassemble but interviews are XML-based; a world can anchor 'convert this court form + statute into a working interview' tasks; grading via fixed personas run through the interview and exact-match on assembled form fields. Value is mainly as task-shape/corpus source, not runnable OSS (free but not fully open-source).

items.name: Appellate practice management
items.what_agents_must_do: Perfect and prosecute an appeal: calendar the notice-of-appeal deadline (30 days from judgment in federal civil, 14 for cross-appeal, tolling by post-judgment motions), file the notice, order transcripts, designate the record, docket the appeal, compute the briefing chain (opening 40 days from record filing, response 30, reply 21 under FRAP default or circuit scheduling order), check brief compliance (word limits, certificate of compliance/service, appendix contents), and track oral argument and mandate.
task_families: notice-of-appeal deadline computation with tolling motions
briefing schedule computation and recalculation on extensions
brief compliance checking (word count, certificates, appendix)
items.world_requirements: Tables: appeals (case, court below, judgment_date, NOA filed_date, appellate case_no, status), tolling_motions (type, filed, decided — changes NOA deadline), briefing_deadlines, transcript_orders, record_designations, compliance_checklists (word_count, certificates booleans). Rule data: FRAP time table + one or two circuit variants. Task shapes: judgment entered date X with a Rule 59 motion decided date Y → compute correct NOA deadline (tolling logic is a classic boundary case) and the full briefing chain; check a brief metadata record against limits; deterministic date/limit verification.

items.name: Calendaring / docketing with court-rule deadlines
items.what_agents_must_do: From a trigger event (complaint served, order entered, trial date set), compute the full downstream deadline chain under the governing rule set (FRCP 6 day-counting: skip trigger day, weekend/holiday roll-forward, +3 days for mail service, court days vs calendar days per jurisdiction), create calendar/docket entries with reminders for assigned attorneys, and recompute the entire chain when a trigger date moves (continuance, amended order).
items.world_requirements: Tables: docket_events (matter, trigger_type, trigger_date), deadlines (event, rule cite, computed_date, assigned_to, status), court_rules (rule set per jurisdiction: offset days, day type, service-method adders), holidays calendar. Tools: deadline calculator, calendar CRUD, rule lookup. Task shapes: serve a complaint on date X in jurisdiction Y → agent must produce the exact gold set of dated deadlines (answer due, initial disclosures, expert disclosure 90 days pre-trial, dispositive motion cutoff); then move the trial date and verify every dependent deadline was recomputed. Fully deterministic verification — the strongest fit in the whole list for programmatic grading.

items.name: Client intake + conflicts checking
items.what_agents_must_do: Run the full intake funnel: capture a lead, collect an intake form, search every party/adverse-party/related-entity name against the firm's contacts, matters, calendar entries, notes and documents (including fuzzy/alias matches), flag hits, route flagged conflicts to a resolution decision (decline, waiver letter, ethical screen), and only then allow matter opening. The concrete capability is exhaustive multi-table name search plus a correct block/allow decision recorded before any work occurs.
items.world_requirements: Tables: contacts (persons + entities with aliases, former names, corporate family links), matters (with party roles: client, adverse, co-party, witness), leads/intake_forms, conflict_checks (search terms, hits, resolution, timestamp, resolver), waivers. Tools: name search with fuzzy matching over all tables; conflict-check record creation; matter-open action that must be gated on a completed clean/resolved check. Task shapes: seed a latent conflict (subsidiary of an existing adverse party, former client under a maiden name) and verify the agent finds it, records the hit, and blocks or waives before opening; deterministic verification = conflict_checks row exists, hit list matches gold, matter status correct.

items.name: CLOC Core 12 (legal operations competency framework)
items.what_agents_must_do: Not a benchmark but the canonical taxonomy of legal-department operations work: Business Intelligence, Financial Management (e-billing/spend), Firm & Vendor Management, Information Governance, Knowledge Management, Org Health, Practice Operations, Project Management, Service Delivery, Strategic Planning, Technology, Training. Defines the non-lawyering task lines a law-firm/legal-dept world should contain.
items.size: 12 functions x 4 maturity stages + Maturity Assessment Playbook
items.world_requirements: Tables for invoices (UTBMS/LEDES billing codes!), timekeepers, rates, matters, vendors, budgets. Deterministic task family: audit LEDES invoice lines against outside-counsel billing guidelines (block billing, rate caps, staffing limits) — exact rule-violation lists are machine-gradable. CLOC maturity language supplies realistic scenario framing.

items.name: Closing binders / transaction closing management
items.what_agents_must_do: Run a deal closing: maintain the live closing checklist (every document/condition by workstream, responsible party, status draft/agreed/executed/delivered), manage signature packets (which signatories sign which pages of which documents, collect and release signatures into escrow), verify all conditions precedent satisfied before closing, compile executed documents with all exhibits/attachments into the final closing binder with index, and distribute it.
task_families: closing checklist creation and status tracking
executed-document compilation (signature pages merged, exhibits attached)
items.world_requirements: Tables: deals (parties, target close date, status), checklist_items (document, workstream, responsible, status, CP flag), signatories, signature_pages (doc × signer, status collected/released), binder_index. Documents: a corpus of deal documents in versions (unsigned drafts, signature pages, exhibits) so compilation is a real file operation. Task shapes: pre-closing audit — identify the 2 seeded unmet CPs and the missing signature page and block closing; assemble the binder whose index and file set must exactly match gold (every executed doc complete with its exhibits); verification = checklist state machine + file-manifest diff.

items.name: Contract Lifecycle Management stage model + OpenCLM
items.what_agents_must_do: Operate the CLM pipeline: intake request → draft from template/clause library → negotiation redlines → approval routing per authority matrix → execution/signature → obligation extraction and deadline tracking → renewal/expiry management.
items.size: OpenCLM: AGPL v3 software (self-hosted contracts, approvals, e-signature, clause libraries, obligations, analytics)
items.world_requirements: Tables: contract records with lifecycle status enum, clause library, approval matrix (role x contract-type x value thresholds), obligations (party, action, due date), counterparties. Tools: draft/redline editors, route-for-approval, e-sign stub. Grading: status-transition legality is machine-checkable (did the agent skip a required approver?), obligation rows exact-match vs gold. Complements Harvey LAB's contracting family with process-state verification instead of LLM-judged prose.

items.name: Court e-filing (CM/ECF)
items.what_agents_must_do: File a document in the correct case: select case and correct docket event type, attach the main document plus exhibits as compliant PDFs (page limits, redaction of PII per FRCP 5.2), pay any fee, receive the Notice of Electronic Filing (NEF) which effects service on registered counsel, docket the filing internally, calendar deadlines the filing triggers, and handle rejection/deficiency notices by re-filing.
task_families: incoming NEF triage into docket + deadlines
items.world_requirements: Tables: court_dockets (case_no, entries with number/date/type/filer/text), filings (status draft/submitted/accepted/rejected + rejection reason), service_lists, NEF notifications queue, fee ledger. Simulated ECF tool: submit(case, event_type, docs) → validates event-type match, PDF/redaction flags, returns NEF or deficiency; incoming-NEF feed the agent must triage. Task shapes: file an opposition brief before the midnight deadline choosing the right event code; process an inbound NEF (order granting motion) into internal docket entries plus the recomputed deadline chain; verification = docket rows and deadline rows vs gold, rejection loop handled.

items.name: Deposition management
items.what_agents_must_do: Schedule a deposition: serve a notice (party deponent) or subpoena (non-party) with correct content and lead time, book court reporter/videographer and location, coordinate availability, track the discovery-cutoff constraint; afterward, receive the transcript, manage the read-and-sign/errata window (30 days in federal practice), log errata by page/line, track exhibits marked, and file a deposition summary.
task_families: notice vs subpoena selection and drafting
scheduling against availability and discovery cutoff
items.world_requirements: Tables: depositions (matter, deponent, party/non-party flag, date, location, status), notices/subpoenas (served_date, method), vendors/bookings, transcripts (received_date, errata_due, errata entries page/line/change), depo_exhibits (number, description, source doc), witness availability calendar. Documents: notice/subpoena templates, a transcript text for summarization tasks. Task shapes: set up a third-party deposition (must choose subpoena, not notice, and calendar it before the discovery cutoff), then process an errata sheet into the transcript record; verification = correct instrument type, dates inside cutoff, errata rows match gold.

items.name: Discovery management (requests, responses, privilege logs, meet-and-confer)
items.what_agents_must_do: Track each served discovery set (interrogatories, RFPs, RFAs) with its 30-day (+ service-method) response deadline; draft request-by-request responses that produce, object with specificity, or state inability to comply; review documents for responsiveness and privilege; build a privilege log with date, author, recipients, privilege basis, and non-generic description for every withheld document; number and record productions (Bates ranges, date, recipient); run meet-and-confer before any motion to compel and track the 45-day motion deadline.
task_families: meet-and-confer letter drafting and dispute tracking
items.world_requirements: Tables: discovery_sets (type, served_date, service_method, response_due, status), requests (set_id, number, text, response, objections), documents corpus (custodian, date, author, recipients, privilege flags — gold labels hidden), privilege_log (doc, date, author, recipients, basis, description), productions (Bates start/end, date, volume), disputes/meet_confer_log. Documents: seeded corpus of ~50-200 matter documents including attorney-client emails, work product drafts, and non-privileged lookalikes. Task shapes: respond to a 25-request RFP set — verifier checks every withheld gold-privileged doc appears on the log with adequate fields, no privileged doc in the production Bates range, response served before computed deadline. Mix of deterministic (deadlines, Bates, log completeness) and rubric (objection quality) grading.

items.name: docassemble
items.what_agents_must_do: Author and run guided interviews in YAML/Python/Markdown: question logic, conditional branching, jurisdiction-specific rules, multi-document assembly to PDF/DOCX. Agent tasks: build a working interview from a form + spec, or complete an interview as a user to produce a correct filed document.
items.size: platform; thousands of public interviews
items.world_requirements: A docassemble server (or emulated interview runtime) as a world service; client-fact tables to feed interviews; gold output documents. Grading is deterministic: run the interview with fixed answer sets and diff assembled document fields against gold. ALKiln (below) supplies the exact test format.

items.name: Document management with versioning and ethical walls
items.what_agents_must_do: File documents into matter-centric workspaces with profile metadata (client, matter, doc type, author), maintain version chains via check-out/check-in (no editing a checked-out doc, new version on check-in), file emails to matters, enforce ethical walls (screened users cannot read/list walled matters), apply per-matter retention policies, and leave a complete audit trail.
task_families: ethical-wall setup after lateral hire or conflict waiver
items.world_requirements: Tables: documents (workspace/matter, doc_id, version_no, checked_out_by, profile metadata), workspaces, access_control (walls: user/group × matter deny rules), audit_log (user, doc, action, timestamp), retention_policies. Tools: file/checkout/checkin, search constrained by ACL, wall creation, audit query. Task shapes: erect an ethical wall around matter X for screened attorney Y then prove via audit log no access; reconstruct which version of an agreement was sent to the counterparty on a date from version history; verification = ACL rows, version chain integrity, audit-log query results match gold.

items.name: Engagement letters and fee agreements
items.what_agents_must_do: Generate a scope-correct engagement letter from a template for the specific matter type and fee arrangement (hourly with rate table, flat, contingency percentage, evergreen retainer), send for signature, track execution, collect the retainer into trust, and record scope limitations and non-engagement letters for declined leads.
task_families: engagement letter drafting from template + matter facts
items.world_requirements: Tables: engagement_letters (matter_id, fee_type, rates, scope text, status draft/sent/signed, signed_date), templates library, rate cards per timekeeper/client, trust_transactions (initial retainer deposit). Documents: template .docx with merge fields; gold letters for comparison. Tools: document generation/merge, signature-status update, trust deposit posting. Task shapes: draft letter whose fee terms must match the matter record exactly; verify merge-field values, correct fee clause chosen, retainer deposit row posted to the right client trust ledger; billing later blocked if letter unsigned.

items.name: Expert witness management (FRCP 26(a)(2))
items.what_agents_must_do: Retain and track experts: run a conflict/prior-testimony check, execute an engagement agreement with rates, calendar the disclosure deadline (90 days before trial or per scheduling order; rebuttal 30 days after opposing disclosure), verify the written report contains all six required elements (opinions, facts/data considered, exhibits, qualifications, prior-testimony list for 4 years, compensation), supplement under 26(e), and track opposing-expert Daubert challenge deadlines.
task_families: report completeness check against the six 26(a)(2)(B) elements
items.world_requirements: Tables: experts (name, field, rates, retained_matter, side), expert_engagements (agreement date, budget, invoices), disclosures (type initial/rebuttal, due_date, served_date), report_checklists (six boolean element fields), prior_testimony records, deadlines linkage to scheduling-order table. Documents: a draft expert report with a seeded missing element (e.g., no compensation statement). Task shapes: given a scheduling order and trial date, compute and calendar all expert deadlines and flag the report deficiency; verification = deadline rows exact, checklist booleans match gold defect.

items.name: Juriscraper + RECAP/CourtListener (Free Law Project docket stack)
items.what_agents_must_do: Automated docket monitoring workflow: scrape court sites/PACER for new filings, parse docket sheets and opinions into structured metadata, trigger case alerts, fetch documents on demand — the plumbing of litigation-watch and docketing departments.
task_families: docket sheet parsing to structured entries
items.size: scrapers for 400+ US courts; tens of millions of records; PACER Fetch APIs
items.world_requirements: World needs courts/cases/docket_entries/documents tables with timestamped incoming filings (simulated PACER), an alert-subscription tool, and tasks like 'monitor matter M, docket every new entry, calendar any triggered deadlines'; grading deterministic via exact docket-entry and calendar-row comparison.

items.name: KYC/AML client screening
items.what_agents_must_do: Before (or under strict conditions during) engagement: verify client identity documents, unwrap corporate structures to identify ultimate beneficial owners (>25% thresholds), screen every client/UBO/counterparty against sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media lists, assign a risk rating driving standard vs enhanced due diligence (source of funds/wealth for high risk), record the CDD file, set ongoing-monitoring triggers, and escalate true hits to the MLRO / decline representation for sanctioned parties.
task_families: sanctions/PEP/adverse-media list screening with false-positive adjudication
items.world_requirements: Tables: clients, ownership_edges (entity→owner %, layered so UBO requires graph traversal), screening_lists (sanctions/PEP entries with near-miss name variants), screenings (subject, list hits, adjudication true/false positive, rationale), risk_ratings, cdd_files (documents collected, status), monitoring_alerts. Tools: list-match search (fuzzy), ownership traversal, risk-score computation. Task shapes: onboard a company whose 3-layer ownership hides a 30% sanctioned UBO behind a nominee — agent must traverse to the UBO, adjudicate the near-miss name correctly, rate high-risk, and block engagement; verification = UBO set, hit adjudications, and engagement status vs gold.

items.name: Matter opening (new business intake)
items.what_agents_must_do: Open a matter only after conflicts clear and engagement is signed: assign client/matter numbers, practice area, responsible + billing attorney, staffing, rate card, billing arrangement, LEDES client/matter IDs, court/jurisdiction data, statute-of-limitations date, and create the matter workspace in the DMS plus initial docket entries and tasks.
task_families: matter record creation with required-field validation
items.world_requirements: Tables: matters (number, client_id, practice_area, responsible_atty, billing_atty, status, open_date, SOL_date, jurisdiction, court, billing_arrangement, client_matter_ids for e-billing), users/timekeepers, rate_assignments, tasks, calendar. Gating logic: matter cannot open without clean conflict check + signed engagement letter (referential checks the verifier can assert). Task shapes: given an intake packet, open the matter with every required field correct; deterministic verification against gold matter row; failure modes = missing SOL date, wrong rate card, opening despite unresolved conflict.

items.name: Outside-counsel-guidelines compliance billing (LEDES/UTBMS)
items.what_agents_must_do: Produce e-billing that survives the client's automated rules engine: code every time/expense line with correct UTBMS task (e.g., L240 dispositive motions) and activity (A101-A111) codes, apply the client's OCG rules (no block billing, timekeeper rate caps, staffing restrictions, non-billable categories like intra-office conferences over N attendees, budget/phase caps, pre-approval requirements), assemble a valid pipe-delimited LEDES 1998B file (24 fields per line, header/invoice/matter arithmetic consistent), submit, and process rejections/appeals of reduced lines.
task_families: OCG rule application and violation flagging
accrual and budget reporting to client
items.world_requirements: Tables: time_entries with codes, client_billing_guidelines (machine-readable rule set: banned codes, rate caps per timekeeper class, max hours/day, pre-approval list), ledes_invoices (raw file text + parse status), rejections (line, rule violated), timekeeper classifications. Tools: LEDES validator (field count, delimiter, arithmetic: sum of line totals = invoice total), OCG rules engine simulating the client's e-billing platform. Task shapes: code and export a month of WIP for an OCG client — the simulated e-billing endpoint deterministically rejects any line violating the rule set; agent iterates until acceptance; verification = validator pass + zero gold-rule violations + arithmetic exact. Entirely deterministic and directly reusable as an executable-world verifier.

items.name: Settlement negotiation tracking
items.what_agents_must_do: Maintain the negotiation ledger of a dispute: log each demand and offer (party, amount, terms, date, expiry, response), compute deltas and authority limits (client-approved settlement authority vs current offer), track mediation sessions and Rule 68 offers of judgment with their cost-shifting deadlines, draft settlement agreements and releases reflecting the final agreed terms, and generate the settlement disbursement sheet (gross, fees, costs, liens, net to client) that feeds trust accounting.
task_families: settlement agreement drafting from negotiated terms
items.world_requirements: Tables: negotiations (matter, round, direction demand/offer, amount, terms, date, expiry, status), settlement_authority (client-approved floor/ceiling, date), liens (medical, subrogation amounts), settlements (final amount, terms), disbursements linking to trust ledger. Documents: settlement agreement/release templates. Task shapes: log a counteroffer and detect it exceeds authority → must seek client instruction rather than accept; compute a disbursement sheet where contingency fee %, costs, and liens must reconcile to the gross settlement to the penny and post correctly to trust; arithmetic and state-machine verification are fully deterministic.

items.name: Suffolk Document Assembly Line (court-form interview library)
items.what_agents_must_do: Open library of production court-form interviews built on docassemble with a shared component framework (AssemblyLine package, ALToolbox, EFSP e-filing integration). Concrete multi-step shape: intake → eligibility screen → form completion → assembly → e-file.
items.size: 100+ open-source court-form interviews (MA and beyond), quarterly-updated
items.world_requirements: Import real interview YAML as world content; simulated e-filing endpoint (accepts packet, validates required fields/signatures/fees); grade on packet-field exactness vs gold. Provides realistic pro-bono/clinic task lines for a law-firm world.

items.name: TARexp (eugene-yang/tarexp)
items.what_agents_must_do: Python framework declaratively composing TAR workflows: seed selection → classifier training → batch selection (CAL/SAL) → labeling → stopping-rule evaluation, with cost-based metrics (OptimisticCost, cost dynamics) and built-in stopping rules (Budget, QBCB, Kneedle, etc.).
items.size: framework (used with TREC/RCV1 collections)
items.world_requirements: Host as tasks where the agent operates a review campaign: tables for review batches, per-doc predicted scores, reviewer labels, per-hour review cost; agent must decide batch sizes and certify a defensible stopping point; grade deterministically on achieved recall vs cost against TARexp-computed optimal frontier.

items.name: Time capture, prebill review, and invoicing
items.what_agents_must_do: Record time entries (timekeeper, matter, date, hours, narrative, task/activity codes), run the monthly cutoff, generate prebills/proformas per matter, review entries for vague narratives, block billing, duplicates, wrong rates and guideline violations, apply write-downs/write-offs with reasons, obtain billing-attorney approval, and issue final invoices; compute realization and WIP/AR metrics.
items.world_requirements: Tables: time_entries (timekeeper, matter, date, hours, rate, narrative, task_code, activity_code, status unbilled/billed/written_off), expense_entries, prebills (line adjustments with reason codes), invoices (header + lines, totals, status), payments/AR, rate_cards with effective dates. Tools: prebill generation, line-item edit/write-down, invoice issue, aging report. Task shapes: generate the prebill for matter M for month N, catch the 3 seeded defects (duplicate entry, rate mismatch vs engagement letter, block-billed narrative), apply specified adjustments, issue invoice whose arithmetic and line set match gold; verification = exact table diff.

items.name: Trust / IOLTA accounting with three-way reconciliation
items.what_agents_must_do: Maintain per-client trust sub-ledgers and a master trust ledger; post retainer deposits, disburse settlements, transfer earned fees to operating only after invoicing; monthly, reconcile three records to the penny — adjusted bank statement balance (ending balance ± outstanding checks/deposits in transit), trust book ledger, and the sum of all client sub-ledgers — and identify/correct any discrepancy (commingling, ledger overdraft, misposted client, stale check) without ever letting a client ledger go negative.
items.world_requirements: Tables: trust_bank_transactions (bank-side statement lines), trust_ledger (book side: date, client, matter, payee, amount, check_no, cleared flag), client_trust_subledgers derived per client, operating_account, reconciliations (period, three balances, status, discrepancy notes). Tools: post transaction, mark cleared, run reconciliation report, transfer trust→operating. Task shapes: month-end close with seeded discrepancies (a $150 check posted to the wrong client, a deposit in transit, a disbursement exceeding one client's balance) — agent must produce a reconciliation where all three totals match and name each correcting entry. Penny-exact deterministic verification; the canonical flaky-boundary task since one wrong ledger row breaks the invariant sum(subledgers)=book=adjusted bank.

items.name: awesome-legal-skills (lawve-ai)
