items.size: 238+ agent skills across 24 practice areas
items.world_requirements: Not a benchmark but the richest open catalog of agentic legal task procedures found; a world can mine its skill procedures as task specs (each skill's step list becomes the gold process) — hosting needs whatever each skill touches: matter tables, disclosure bundles, playbooks, billing records.

items.name: ContraxSuite + LexNLP (LexPredict)
items.what_agents_must_do: Open-source contract analytics: LexNLP extracts dates, amounts, durations, courts, citations, definitions, and clauses from unstructured legal text; ContraxSuite wraps it in a document-exploration/review platform with clustering and classification.
items.size: OSS (AGPL): extraction of 20+ entity kinds, hundreds of clause types, pretrained models

items.name: Court-deadline computation rules engines (CalendarRules / DocketCalendar / Aderant Milana / courtdeadlinecalculator.org)
items.what_agents_must_do: Given a trigger event (service of complaint, order entered), compute all downstream deadlines by applying jurisdiction rules: FRCP 6-style day counting, calendar vs court days, weekend/holiday rollover, service-method extensions (+3 mail days), local-rule overrides — then calendar them.
task_families: deadline chain computation from trigger events
items.size: commercial rule sets covering federal + state courts; no full OSS engine found
items.world_requirements: The single best deterministic task family for a law-firm world: tables for court rules (rule id, trigger, offset days, day-type, rollover policy), holiday calendars per jurisdiction, service events, and a firm calendar; gold answers are exactly computable dates. No open-source engine exists, so the world must implement its own small rules engine — cheap, and grading is pure date equality. Boundary cases (holiday clusters, backward-counted deadlines) give natural flaky-task boundaries.

items.name: eyecite (Free Law Project)
items.what_agents_must_do: Extract and resolve legal citations from any text: full citations (Bush v. Gore, 531 U.S. 98), short forms (531 U.S., at 99), supra, id., ibid.; resolves them to reporter entries; used to annotate CourtListener/CAP corpora. Anchors cite-checking tasks: verify every citation in a brief exists, is well-formed, and resolves to the right case.
items.size: library; tested against 55M+ citations
items.world_requirements: World needs a briefs/memos document store, a citation reference table (valid reporter/volume/page tuples derived from the world's case corpus), and eyecite itself as the deterministic verifier: agent-flagged bad citations diffed against seeded errors. Ideal boundary-provable flaky-task material (seed N bad cites, require exactly those N found).

items.name: FreeEed (shmsoft/FreeEed)
items.what_agents_must_do: Open-source eDiscovery engine (Tika+Lucene+Solr+OCR): culling, text/metadata extraction, indexing, keyword search, review UI, and load-file export — the concrete open reference implementation of an EDRM processing+review pipeline a simulated firm can mirror.
items.size: open-source platform; processes 1,400+ file types
items.world_requirements: Defines the tool surface a world should expose: staging area for raw evidence, processing job queue with parameters (dedupe on/off, OCR, date filters), full-text search endpoint, tag/production-set tables. Task shape: 'process custodian X, apply search terms from the ESI protocol, produce set PROD001'; grade on exact doc-id membership of the production set.

items.name: LRAGE (Legal RAG Evaluation toolkit)
items.what_agents_must_do: Harness, not tasks: runs LLMs and autonomous agents in legal RAG settings against pluggable retrievers/rerankers/corpora with lm-eval-harness-style scoring, including agentic evaluation via smolagents.
items.size: toolkit; integrates Pile-of-Law, LegalBench, LawBench, KBL corpora; smolagents integration
items.world_requirements: Reusable infrastructure: the firm world can mount its own document corpus and task set into LRAGE to get retrieval-ablated scoring (same task with/without gold retrieval) for free — useful for boundary-proving whether a flaky task fails on retrieval or reasoning.

items.name: TAR Evaluation Toolkit / BMI (Cormack-Grossman Baseline Model Implementation)
items.what_agents_must_do: Reference autonomous TAR baseline: runs CAL end-to-end (logistic regression over token features, relevance feedback loop) that any agentic reviewer must beat; used as the TREC Total Recall baseline system.
items.size: VM + scripts; baseline for Total Recall tracks
items.world_requirements: Only needs the same oracle+corpus scaffolding as Total Recall; useful in the world as the published 'beat the baseline' bar for e-discovery tasks (agent recall@effort vs BMI recall@effort).
